slides.heading: Boggle Board
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Boggle Board, a hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Which words can be formed by chaining 8-directionally adjacent letters without reusing a cell?
Trie of words + DFS from every cell.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Which words can be formed by chaining 8-directionally adjacent letters without reusing a cell? Trie of words plus DFS from every cell.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A trie of the words lets the board DFS prune paths that can't spell any word.
slides.narration: A trie of the words lets the board DFS prune paths that can't spell any word.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Search each word separately on the board → O(words · cells · 8^L)
Trie + single DFS from each cell → prunes shared prefixes
Mark cells used on the current path
slides.narration: Searching for each word separately repeats work for shared prefixes. A trie of all words lets one DFS from each cell explore them together and prune early.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. DFS from every cell along trie edges
slides.narration: Step by step. First, insert words into a trie. Second, dFS from every cell along trie edges. Third, mark visited cells. Fourth, record words at word-end markers.

slides.caption: Prune when the trie has no branch
slides.narration: Any time the trie has no branch for the next letter, we stop exploring that path. That pruning is what makes it fast.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/2)
slides.narration: We build a trie with words at terminal nodes. DFS from every cell follows the trie child for the cell's letter, records any word, marks the cell, recurses in eight directions, then unmarks it.

slides.narration: We build a trie with words at terminal nodes. DFS from every cell follows the trie child for the cell's letter, records any word, marks the cell, recurses in eight directions, then unmarks it.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of ws plus w times h times 8 to the s. Space is O of ws plus w times h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Don't reuse a cell in one word
slides.narration: Moves include diagonals, a cell can't be reused in one word, and the same word may be found twice.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: remove found words from the trie
slides.narration: Explain the pruning. Removing found words from the trie speeds things up further.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A trie of the words lets the board DFS prune paths that can't spell any word.
slides.narration: To recap Boggle Board: A trie of the words lets the board DFS prune paths that can't spell any word. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
